stem: A bus company runs a 45-seat bus from Peshawar to Islamabad. Each ticket costs 850 rupees, and the company needs at least 25,000 rupees in ticket sales from a trip to cover the cost of the trip. Which of the following gives all possible numbers of tickets \(t\) the company can sell for one trip that covers its cost?
solution: Ticket sales of \(t\) tickets are \(850t\) rupees, so \(850t \ge 25{,}000\) gives \(t \ge 29.4\).
The number of tickets is a whole number, so at least 30 tickets must be sold (29 tickets bring in only 24,650 rupees).
The bus has 45 seats, so \(t \le 45\). Together, \(30 \le t \le 45\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. \(850 \times 29 = 24{,}650\), which is less than 25,000. Rounding 29.4 down gives a number of tickets that does not cover the cost.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This ignores the 45 seats on the bus; more than 45 tickets cannot be sold.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This reverses the inequality: these are the numbers of tickets that do NOT cover the cost.
explanation.D: Correct. At least 30 tickets (since \(850 \times 30 = 25{,}500\)) and at most 45 tickets.

verify:
ok = [k for k in range(0, 46) if 850*k >= 25000]
assert ok == list(range(30, 46))
parts = choices[answer].strip('\\() ').split('\\le')
assert len(parts) == 3 and Rational(parts[0]) == 30 and Rational(parts[2]) == 45 and parts[1].strip() == 't'
assert all(choices[k] != choices[answer] for k in choices if k != answer)
